screening_decisions.reason: This observational study examines genetic factors (alpha-thalassemia co-inheritance) affecting hematological indices in SCD patients. It does not evaluate RBC transfusion as an intervention. The study focuses on genotype-phenotype correlations rather than transfusion therapy.

This RCT evaluates hydroxycarbamide (hydroxyurea) versus placebo in young children with SCD. While transfusions are mentioned as a secondary outcome measure, the primary intervention is pharmacological, not RBC transfusion. Does not meet the intervention criterion.

This is a narrative review about iron overload management in transfused SCD patients. It discusses transfusion regimes descriptively but does not compare transfusion vs no transfusion or restrictive vs liberal strategies. Focuses on chelation therapy rather than transfusion efficacy.
General review article covering molecular basis and advances in SCD understanding. Does not specifically address RBC transfusion interventions or compare transfusion strategies.
Methodological paper about conducting overviews of systematic reviews. Not related to SCD or RBC transfusion interventions. Irrelevant to the review topic.

RCT comparing regular blood transfusions vs standard care (observation) in children with SCD and silent cerebral infarcts. Directly addresses transfusion intervention for preventing stroke recurrence. Meets all PICO criteria: SCD population, RBC transfusion intervention, comparison with no transfusion, outcome of cerebral infarct prevention.

RCT comparing prophylactic transfusions vs transfusions only for emergencies in pregnant women with SCD. Evaluates whether routine prophylactic transfusion improves maternal/fetal outcomes. Meets criteria: SCD population, RBC transfusion intervention, clear comparison group, outcomes include painful crises and complications.

RCT comparing preoperative transfusion vs no preoperative transfusion in SCD patients undergoing surgery. Evaluates perioperative complication rates. Meets all criteria: SCD population, RBC transfusion intervention, comparison with no transfusion, outcomes include acute chest syndrome and other complications.

Feasibility study focused on validating sPLA2 as a biomarker for predicting ACS. Only 10 patients were randomized to transfusion vs observation; the primary aim was biomarker validation, not evaluating transfusion efficacy. Too limited as a transfusion intervention study.
Commentary/article discussing management challenges in developing countries. Not a primary study evaluating RBC transfusion interventions. Does not provide evidence on transfusion effectiveness.
Review article about pathophysiological mechanisms (coagulation and inflammation) in SCD. Does not evaluate RBC transfusion interventions or compare transfusion strategies.
Methodological guidance document for systematic review reporting. Not related to SCD or RBC transfusion interventions. Irrelevant to the review topic.

Single case report about sleep apnea in one SCD patient. Mentions history of transfusions but does not evaluate transfusion as an intervention. Not suitable for systematic review of transfusion effectiveness.

In vitro laboratory study measuring blood viscosity in mixtures of sickle and normal cells. While it discusses transfusion implications, it is mechanistic research, not a clinical study evaluating transfusion outcomes in patients.

Case series of 6 patients with cerebrovascular disease and pulmonary hypertension. Describes associations but does not evaluate RBC transfusion as an intervention. No comparison group for transfusion strategies.
Epidemiological study mapping global distribution of sickle hemoglobin. Provides population estimates but does not evaluate RBC transfusion interventions or their effectiveness.

Observational study describing alloimmunization prevalence in transfused SCD patients. While related to transfusion safety, it does not compare transfusion vs no transfusion or different transfusion strategies. Descriptive rather than interventional.
RCT evaluating isoxsuprine (vasodilator drug) for leg ulcer healing in SCD. The intervention is pharmacological, not RBC transfusion. Does not meet the intervention criterion.
RCT evaluating topical RGD peptide matrix for leg ulcer healing in SCD. The intervention is a topical treatment, not RBC transfusion. Does not meet the intervention criterion.

Phase 3 RCT comparing chronic transfusion vs hydroxycarbamide in children with SCD and abnormal TCD velocities. One arm receives standard transfusions (maintaining <30% HbS), providing direct evidence on transfusion effectiveness for stroke prevention. Meets criteria: SCD population, RBC transfusion intervention, comparison with alternative treatment, outcome of TCD velocity/stroke prevention.
This is a Phase II clinical trial about Arginine Butyrate treatment for sickle cell leg ulcers, not a Cochrane Review. The intervention studied is not RBC transfusion.

This is a primary multicenter research study published in NEJM comparing transfusion regimens, not a Cochrane Review. While it addresses RBC transfusions for SCD, it does not meet the study design criterion.
This is a review article from ashpublications.org about red cell exchange transfusions, not a Cochrane Review.
This is a general overview article about sickle cell disease pathophysiology and management, not a Cochrane Review focused on RBC transfusions.
This is a general review article from The Lancet about sickle cell disease, not a Cochrane Review.
This is an epidemiology article about migration and SCD incidence, not a Cochrane Review about RBC transfusions.
This is a genetics article about genetic modifiers of SCD phenotype, not a Cochrane Review about RBC transfusions.
This is a primary randomized clinical trial evaluating pre-operative transfusion practices, not a Cochrane Review.
This is a primary randomized clinical trial published in NEJM about transfusions for stroke prevention, not a Cochrane Review.
This is a phase 3 randomized clinical trial (SWiTCH) comparing transfusion/chelation to hydroxyurea/phlebotomy, not a Cochrane Review.
This is a cohort study about LDH as a biomarker in SCD, not a Cochrane Review about RBC transfusions.
This is a review article from ashpublications.org summarizing transfusion management, but it is not a Cochrane Review.
This is a placebo-controlled clinical trial about Cajanus cajan extract, not a Cochrane Review about RBC transfusions.
This is a randomized prospective study about hip core decompression for osteonecrosis in SCD, not a Cochrane Review about RBC transfusions.
This is a methodological paper about developing the AMSTAR tool for assessing systematic reviews, not a Cochrane Review about RBC transfusions for SCD.
This is a cross-sectional study about HIV transmission risk in transfused children with SCD, not a Cochrane Review.
This is a randomized controlled trial about topical treatments for sickle cell ulcers, not a Cochrane Review about RBC transfusions.
